topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section outlines the lecture's learning objectives, introduces the hallmarks of cancer framework, and establishes the model of multistep tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases, drive autonomous proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how malignant cells fail to execute terminal differentiation programs, comparing hematopoietic lineages with intestinal epithelial renewal in colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells circumvent programmed cell death through disruptions in p53 regulation and shifts in the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms of telomere attrition, TERT reactivation, and p53-mediated senescence checkpoints, concluding the discussion on growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the alteration of cancer cell metabolism, covering aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and how metabolic enzyme mutations produce oncometabolites that alter gene expression.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the induction of new blood vessel growth required for tumor nutrient and oxygen supply, including the angiogenic switch and anti-angiogenic strategies.

topics.label: Tumor metastasis and dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the process of systemic cancer spread, including metastatic inefficiency, the seed and soil hypothesis, clinical biomarkers, and genomic analyses of metastases.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarises the key themes of the lecture, reviews the convergence of cancer hallmarks, and directs students to further literature.
